items.title: Jerome Richardson interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, March 9, 1996
items.q: when Charlie Parker showed up I was in San Francisco and I heard all the stuff that Charlie was playing, and he messed up my mind just like he messed up everybody’s mind... everything I played on the alto sounded like Charlie Parker to me. So I said no, I’ll play tenor.

ctx.x: As a matter of fact I’ve got a picture of one of his greatest hits records, and you’re on it playing tenor.

Yeah? Well in those days I came there playing tenor. What had happened with me, when Charlie Parker showed up I was in San Francisco and I heard all the stuff that Charlie was playing, and he messed up my mind just like he messed up everybody’s mind, and I was playing alto then. I said I can’t do this, much as I love Charlie Parker, I just can’t — everything I played on the alto sounded like Charlie Parker to me. So I said no, I’ll play tenor. So that’s how I started playing tenor.
Because there was maybe a little more room for your own thing in there?
